newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Infratil International launches prospectus.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Infratil International launches prospectus.

text.p: Infratil International Ltd, the company jointly bidding for Argentina's postal concession, launched its prospectus on Friday aiming to raise NZ$50 million through a one for two rights issue.

The company has formed a joint venture with state-owned New Zealand Post take part in a consortium bidding for the 30-year concession to run the system. The concession also includes a banking and telecommunications licence.
The joint venture will have a 24 percent interest in the consortium, which involves Citibank N.A. and Argentina's La Caja, a large, family-owned insurance company.
Infratil International is a sister company to those already managed by investment bankers Morrison and Co -- Infratil New Zealand Ltd and Infratil Australia.
All three invest in infrastucture and utilities.

Infratil International has already spent NZ$25 million for an 11.8 percent stake in Pasadena-based Airport Group International (AGI). AGI is part of a consortium that successfully bid for Perth Airport.
AGI's other shareholders include Lockheed Martin, GE Captital, Bechtel Corp, Soros Fund Management, Duty Free Shoppers and SunAmerica.
Infratil NZ shareholders will receive one Infratil International share for every every Infratil NZ share held.

Morrison and Co principal Lloyd Morrison told a briefing of analysts and journalists that NZ Post was highly regarded as an effificent and profitable postal service operator, with consultancy experience in Malaysia, South Korea, Vietnam, Turkey, Portugal, Thailand, South Africa, Namibia and Ireland.

"They are developing their existing skills by applying them to new situations offshore where the circumstances are slightly different and in some cases a lot more challenging," Morrison said. But NZ Post's state ownership meant committing capital to
overseas investments was not possible.

"So it makes a lot of sense for Infratil to come along with its capital, its deal making and stucturing skills and align itself with the management expertise and intellectual capital of NZ Post," he said.
Argentina's postal service, ENCOTESA, had similar turnover to NZ Post but 20,000 staff against NZ Post's 9,300.
NZ shifted 775 million postal units per annum against just 500 million in Argentina but costs per unit were just 28 U.S. cents against 75 cents in Argentina.
"That obviously says there is potential for efficiency gains compared to NZ Post," he said.
Morrison said that with Argentina's population of 34 million, there was also room for volume growth.
Bids for the concession are due on June 3 and an announcement of the successful bidder is expected on July 28.

Infratil International will put in loan capital to cover the cost of the involvement of the joint venture in the consortium and NZ Post will channel part of its management fees into capitalising its share of the 50/50 joint venture.
Morrison said the telecommunications side held possibilities for Citibank.
Citibank, in conjunction with Spain's Telefonica operates Argentina's southern network.
If the consortium wins the concession, the telecommunications licence would allow Citibank and Telefonica to extend into the north via the postal network, Morrison said.
The issue is underwritten by brokers ANZ Securities and Doyle Paterson Brown. Rights trading ends on June 24 and the company expects to list the following day.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
